Netlink tile setup, seccomp, and event loop for link, route, and neighbor updates.

# Purpose
`fd_netlink_tile.c` defines the `netlnk` topology tile that keeps kernel network state in sync with shared-memory tables used by the rest of the system. It creates and joins topology objects for the double-buffered network device table, IPv4 route tables, and the neighbor hash map, then stores the object IDs and interface name in the tile configuration. It also sets the object sizes, alignment, hash seeds, and other properties needed to allocate and join these shared-memory structures.

The file also implements the tile runtime. It opens and binds netlink sockets, sets seccomp and file-descriptor access rules, and runs an event loop through `fd_stem.c`. The tile reads netlink updates for links, routes, and neighbors, marks the needed update actions, and performs full table reloads with backoff control. It also handles neighbor solicit requests by updating the neighbor map and sending probes with rate limiting. Metrics are written for update counts, table sizes, probe activity, and netlink buffer drops.
